views.label: Static
caption: The Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter black hole ($r_s = 2L$, so that $r_h = L$), maximally extended, each point in the diagram a 2-sphere of radius $r$. Its tortoise coordinate $r_*$, with $dr_*/dr = (1 - r_s/r + r^2/L^2)^{-1}$ and $r_*(0) = 0$, tends to a finite value $R = 0.658\,L$ as $r \to \infty$, and the Kruskal coordinates $U = -e^{-\kappa u}$ and $V = e^{\kappa v}$, with $u, v = ct \mp r_*$ and $\kappa = 2/L$, make the metric regular through $r_h$. With $p = \arctan U$ and $q = \arctan V$ the singularity $r = 0$, where $UV = 1$, lies on the horizontal lines $T = \pm\pi/2$, and the conformal boundary, where $UV = -e^{2\kappa R} = -13.9$, on the two timelike curves at the sides.

The coordinates $t$ and $r > r_h$ cover the right exterior alone. The horizon is the pair of null lines $U = 0$ and $V = 0$, crossing at the bifurcation sphere. A light ray that leaves a boundary at $t = 0$ meets $r = 0$ at $X = \pm 1.047$, two thirds of the way from the axis to the corner, so the diagram is wider than the square of the BTZ black hole: with the singularities drawn straight the boundaries bow outward, and the map $U \to U/\sqrt{13.9}$, $V \to V/\sqrt{13.9}$ straightens the boundaries and bows the singularities inward.
legend: the region that $t$ and $r > r_h$ cover

views.label: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein
caption: The Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter black hole ($r_s = 2L$) with the ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $v$ and $r$ on it. From $V = e^{\kappa v}$ and $U = UV(r)/V$, one formula for every $r > 0$, they cover the exterior and the black hole together, and their lines of constant $v$ are ingoing light rays, which leave the conformal boundary, cross the horizon at 45°, and end at $r = 0$.

views.label: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein
caption: The Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter black hole ($r_s = 2L$) with the outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $u$ and $r$ on it, the time reverse of the ingoing ones. From $U = -e^{-\kappa u}$ and $V = UV(r)/U$ they cover the exterior and the white hole, and their lines of constant $u$ are outgoing light rays, which leave $r = 0$, cross the horizon outward, and end on the conformal boundary.
